subject: platform/proposal
professional: a residential remodeling contractor / estimator who sends written proposals every week, backed by a construction-contracts lawyer for the terms. The estimator would first ask: does the printed total, deposit and balance add up to the cent, does the price-held date land on the right day, and can an internal cost ever reach the customer's sheet? The lawyer would first ask: what does the customer's signature on this sheet bind them to, and does the tool warn about statutory deposit caps and licence-number requirements?

evidence.correctness: What it is: a canonical proposal.mjs (buildProposal, renderProposalHtml, scopeLines, money, addDays, referenceFor), a terms.mjs for carrying five terms in a share link, adopt.mjs that wires the proposal into bid calculators from trades.json, and verify.mjs that drives the built page in Chromium. Ran: node --test '*.test.mjs' from platform/proposal. Recomputed independently by hand, not with the author's tests: (1) deposit/balance: 2500 x 33.333% = 833.325 -> 833.33, balance 1666.67 (tool: 833.33 / 1666.67, sum 2500.00); 2734.07 x 50% = 1367.035 -> 1367.04 (tool 1367.04, balance 1367.03); 12345.67 x 30% = 3703.701 -> 3703.70 (tool 3703.7); 0.01 x 50% -> 0.01 / 0.00. All agree. (2) price-held date: 2026-11-07 + 30 d = 2026-12-07; 2026-12-15 + 30 d = 2027-01-14 (16 days left in December); 2028-02-28 + 1 d = 2028-02-29 (leap); all agree; formatDate('2026-11-07') = '7 November 2026'. (3) scopeLines templates: '{n} gate{n+s}' with n=1 -> '1 gate', n=0 -> '0 gates'; '{y~2}' on 48.888888 -> '48.89'; each-rows drop the row whose when-field is 0 and keep 'A 1,600 sf' (all as the README says). (4) HTML escaping: companyName 'X' renders as <b>X, deposit row prints '(33.333%)'. (5) terms round trip: encodeTerms/decodeTerms keep 'a&b=c #d' intact, drop a 513-char note whole, reject depositPercent=-5, NaN, an unknown id and a NUL byte. (6) verify.mjs: built the real site (node platform/pages/build.mjs, ~3 min) then node platform/proposal/verify.mjs on sump-pump, fence, flooring, translator-project-quote, hood-cleaning bid calculators: '1/1' and '4/4 calculators hand the customer a sound proposal' (real Chromium, price on sheet = price on screen, no cost words, no 'undefined'). (7) adopt.mjs --all --dry: '92 adopted, 0 skipped'. Defects found in the CANONICAL file (the vendored venture copies already fix them, see defects): addDays('2026-02-30', 5) returns 2026-03-07 (Feb 30 silently rolled to 2 March); addDays('9999-12-31', 1) returns the malformed '+010000-01'; buildProposal accepts price 1e12 and prints $999,999,999,999,999,900,000.00 for 1e21. Float half-cent: money(1.005) = '$1.00', money(0.145) = '$0.14' where a decimal calculation gives $1.01 / $0.15, while money(2.675) = '$2.68' (inconsistent half-cent handling; only matters for a price not already in whole cents, which the calculators produce). Not 4 because the shipped venture copy and the canonical file disagree and the canonical one is the wrong one.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: printable proposal with scope/deposit/price-held/signature (rendered, verify.mjs passes on 5 real calculators); customer sheet carries no cost (verify.mjs check 4 passes, print CSS hides main); customer name/address never persisted (saveCompany writes COMPANY_FIELDS only, read in proposal.mjs; test exists); deposit + balance = total exactly (checked by hand above); terms in bid link (terms.mjs round trip works); adopt.mjs --list works and reports 120 adopted, 6 blocked (hoarding-cleanout, lawn-aeration-overseeding, liquidation-pallet, sauna-cold-plunge-install, storage-auction-max, water-well-drilling), which agrees with the README's 'does not adopt yet / deliberately' paragraphs for those six. Not working or stale: README says 'biohazard-cleanup is the current holdout' but ventures/biohazard-cleanup-bid-calculator has proposal.mjs, 5 proposal:begin markers and a trades.json entry (adopted); README counts ('112 adopted, 0 blocked', 'closes the set at 102', '27 hand-ported + 74 generated', 'the 48 adopting tools', 'eighty-seven') disagree with each other and with the 120 adopted / 92 trades.json entries / 60 terms copies on disk; adopt.mjs --sync prints 're-vendored proposal.mjs + proposal.test.mjs' and its VENDORED list (adopt.mjs:42) omits terms.mjs although README says terms.mjs is vendored the same way. Feature set is end to end; the sync mechanism the README tells you to use is the broken part.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' (platform/proposal): 108 tests, 105 pass, 3 FAIL on an untouched tree (not caused by me: git status clean for platform/proposal). The three are sync.test.mjs 'every venture copy of proposal.mjs matches' (121 venture copies differ from canonical), 'proposal.test.mjs' (121 differ) and 'proposal-terms.test.mjs' (60 differ). The venture copies are identical to each other (md5 f3797c40... x121), so the canonical file is the stale one: ventures/*/proposal.mjs gained isoStamp calendar validation and a 1e9 price cap (commit 995628ad, #13726, whose title is about shift-roster-builder) without platform/proposal/proposal.mjs being updated. The drift tripwire the README advertises is red, which is the guard working and nobody acting on it. Seeded mutation 1: proposal.mjs buildProposal 'Math.round(price * depositPercent) / 100' -> 'Math.ceil(...)': proposal.test.mjs 39/39 pass, 0 fail; whole suite 105 pass / 3 fail, identical to baseline: NOT CAUGHT (the tests assert deposit+balance = price, which ceil preserves, and only one exact deposit value, 2952.15; the cents-rounding rule the README calls out as the property is untested). Seeded mutation 2: addDays 'stamp +' -> 'stamp + 86_400_000 +' (price held a day too long): proposal.test.mjs 36 pass, 3 FAIL: caught. Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean for platform/proposal. Vendored suite (the code that ships): ventures/fence-bid-calculator node --test proposal.test.mjs proposal-terms.test.mjs: 67/67 pass. Wired in CI by .github/workflows/proposal-module-ci.yml but only on a path filter, so a change elsewhere (as #13726) can leave it red unnoticed.
evidence.craft: Read in full: proposal.mjs, terms.mjs, sync.test.mjs, the usage/dispatch tail of adopt.mjs and verify.mjs header and loader; skimmed trades.json and the tests. Good: pure functions, validation that throws instead of rendering a hole, UTC date arithmetic, HTML escaping on every interpolated field, scopeLines drops lines with missing figures rather than printing 'undefined', verify.mjs drives a real browser and checks every select option. Defects: (1) canonical proposal.mjs is behind its 121 copies (addDays accepts impossible dates; no price ceiling); (2) adopt.mjs:947-958 sync() copies the stale canonical over every venture copy, so following the README ('Fix it here, then copy it out': node platform/proposal/adopt.mjs --sync) as-is would revert the isoStamp and price-cap fixes in 121 calculators, and it ignores terms.mjs; (3) adopt.mjs is a 54 KB string-splicing generator with page-shape regex anchors (the README records four incidents from these anchors) rather than a template; (4) comments are long incident narratives that dwarf the code and carry stale counts; (5) money() rounds via Math.round(abs * 100), which gives float half-cent artefacts (money(1.005) = $1.00); (6) the 'Valid days' and 'Deposit' fields accept 3650 days and 100% with no warning.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'invents no warranty, lien, arbitration or cancellation language' - backed (proposal.mjs renders only typed text plus a caller-supplied disclaimer; test asserts it). 'customer sheet carries no cost' - backed (verify.mjs 4, print rule). 'deposit + balance equals the printed total exactly' - backed by hand (cents computed, balance = remainder). 'sync.test.mjs fails if any venture copy has drifted, which is what keeps a fix from landing in one calculator and not the other' - true but it is red today and the README gives no instruction for the opposite direction (venture fixed first); following the README's sync command would delete fixes. NOT backed: 'As of 2026-09-07 that is 112 adopted, 0 blocked' (today 120 adopted, 6 blocked); 'biohazard-cleanup is the current holdout' (it is adopted); '27 hand-ported, remaining 74 generated' (92 trades.json entries, 120 adopted); 'terms.mjs is vendored into the 12 calculators that carry the terms without the shared bid spec' (60 proposal-terms.mjs copies on disk); 'All 100 adopters shipped without [featureList]' is history, fine. The README is a 37 KB dated incident log; there is no short statement of what the output is and is not, and the disclaimer lives in each page's generated PROPOSAL_DISCLAIMER, not on this README. Limits stated: not a contract, jurisdiction-dependent terms left to the contractor.
evidence.fitness: Job: a contractor prices a job in a calculator, types business name and customer name, clicks Print proposal, hands over a PDF. Walked through for 5 calculators in Chromium via verify.mjs: the sheet shows the scope, price, deposit and balance, price-held date, signature line, and hides the contractor's cost panel and saved wage/margin rates; clean fallbacks (empty not-included block is omitted; no deposit row at 0%). A real contractor would use it. Gaps they would hit in the first hour: no line items or tax line (a total only for most trades), no change-order or allowance language (by design), no PDF other than the browser print, no company logo, no check that the licence field is filled for states that require it on every proposal, no warning that the 30% default deposit is over some states' home-improvement limits.
evidence.domain: Compared against what a remodeling contractor and a construction-contracts lawyer expect from a written proposal: scope, exclusions, price, payment schedule, validity date, signature, licence number. Matches: exclusions list, validity date, deposit/balance split, licence line, signature and date, plus the explicit decision not to draft warranty, lien, arbitration or cancellation text. Departures: (1) a proposal with a customer signature line becomes the contract in most states the moment it is signed, yet the README says it is 'Deliberately NOT a contract' and nothing on the sheet says what the signature means (accept the scope and price, or enter a contract); (2) state home-improvement statutes cap deposits (for example California Bus. & Prof. Code 7159.5: the lesser of 10% or $1,000 for home improvement contracts) and require specific notices, and several require the licence number in every advertisement or proposal; the tool defaults to 30%, lets the user type up to 100%, and only the disclaimer mentions jurisdiction; (3) no right-to-cancel notice field (the FTC three-day rule for door-to-door sales); none of these is a code defect, but a lawyer would ask for at least a deposit warning and a licence-required prompt; (4) price 'held until' a date is stated but the sheet does not say what happens after; (5) the non-US currency fix (money(value, currency)) is correct for a translator's quote.

defects.what: The canonical file is behind its 121 vendored copies: addDays accepts impossible dates (addDays('2026-02-30', 5) returns 2026-03-07) and malformed years (addDays('9999-12-31', 1) returns '+010000-01'), and buildProposal has no price ceiling (price 1e21 prints $999,999,999,999,999,900,000.00). The copies fixed this (isoStamp, max 1e9, commit 995628ad / #13726) but platform/proposal/proposal.mjs was not updated, so 3 of 108 tests in this directory are red on an untouched tree and 'node platform/proposal/adopt.mjs --sync', the README's own instructions, would overwrite the fixes in 121 live calculators with the stale canonical. Same direction of drift for terms.test.mjs (2 tests missing from 60 venture copies, the other direction).

Seeded mutation Math.round -> Math.ceil on the deposit cents rounding is not caught by any test (39/39 pass in proposal.test.mjs; full suite unchanged at 105 pass / 3 fail). The tests assert deposit + balance = price and one exact deposit (2952.15); the rounding rule the README names as a property is not pinned.

README counts and status are stale and contradict each other: 'current holdout biohazard-cleanup' is adopted; '112 adopted, 0 blocked' vs 120 adopted and 6 blocked; '27 hand-ported + 74 generated' vs 92 trades.json entries; 'the 12 calculators' vs 60 proposal-terms.mjs copies; 'adopt.mjs --sync' output and VENDORED list omit terms.mjs.

No deposit or licence guard: default deposit is 30%, up to 100% is accepted, and there is no warning for statutory home-improvement deposit caps or for a missing licence number; the sheet has a signature line but no statement of what signing means, while the README calls it 'not a contract'.

money() uses Math.round(abs*100): float half-cent artefacts (money(1.005) = $1.00, money(0.145) = $0.14, but money(2.675) = $2.68). Harmless for calculator prices already in cents; a hand-typed fractional price could print one cent off a decimal calculation.
CI for the module runs only on a path filter, so a PR that edits the venture copies without the canonical (or the reverse) goes in with the sync tests red.

verdict: platform/proposal turns a finished bid into a printable customer proposal and it works: the shipped (vendored) code recomputed by hand to the cent on deposit and balance (833.33 + 1666.67 = 2500.00), price-held dates (including leap day and year end), scope pluralisation, rounding and HTML escaping, the terms link round trip is correct, and verify.mjs drove 5 real calculators in Chromium and found a sound sheet with no cost leakage. It does not meet the bar because the guard around the shared code is red and the canonical source is wrong: 3 of 108 tests fail on an untouched tree because 121 venture copies carry a calendar-validation and price-cap fix that the canonical file lacks, and the README's own sync command would roll those fixes back in 121 live calculators. A seeded Math.round -> Math.ceil on the deposit passed every test, the README's counts (112 adopted, 27 + 74, 12 terms copies, biohazard as the holdout) are all stale, and a contracts lawyer would ask for a deposit-cap and licence warning and a statement of what the signature binds. Finished (120 adopted, 6 blocked deliberately), useful to a contractor, not yet at the senior professional bar on verification, claims and domain. Smallest fix: copy ventures/fence-bid-calculator/proposal.mjs into platform/proposal/proposal.mjs, add a fractional-deposit exact-value test, and add terms.mjs to adopt.mjs VENDORED.
